reader.requirement: At --std 85, when any GIVING file-name-3 of a SORT is an indexed file, the compiler must refuse the SORT unless the first KEY data-name is under an ASCENDING phrase and occupies the same character positions in its record as the prime record key of that file (same start and same length); a DESCENDING later key, or a first key in another record description of the SD at those positions, stays legal.

edition-consulted.switches: Year < 2002: SAME RECORD AREA bar on GIVING files (SR9, a different rule) on the same bind path
Format-2 table SORT gate, not reached by a Format-1 SORT with GIVING

reader.edition-search: ScreenIndexedGivingKey itself consults no edition; grep Edition in SortBinder.cs gives only ScreenSameClauses
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises only the legal half (ASCENDING key on the prime key's bytes); none of the refusals

reader.notes: One screen compares keys[0]'s direction, record offset and length with the prime key's window for every indexed GIVING file; it consults no edition and the 1985 'same character positions' reading matches. At --std 85 the COBOL1757 message cites 'ISO §2023:14.9.40.3 SR9' rather than the 1985 rule number, a citation-only blemish.

refuter.evidence: K1alt-001: first key on the ALTERNATE key's bytes 1..2, prime IK at 3..4, DYNAMIC access: refused COBOL1757. K4fdrec2-001: prime key in the FD's second 01 at bytes 3..4, SD key at 3..4: compiled, GIVING file read back in key order (A0ww C3xx A1yy B2zz by bytes 3..4). K5fdrec2bad-001: same FD, SD key at 1..2: refused COBOL1757. K3bgroup-001: group prime key over two PIC X, elementary qualified 'SK OF SR': legal, ordered. K6redef-001: key a REDEFINES of bytes 1..2 with 'ON ASCENDING SK' (KEY omitted): legal, ordered. K2bclass-001: SD key PIC 99 over prime PIC XX positions: compiles (positions only). K3group-001 (RANDOM access) refused for the separate 1985 ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM rule, not this one. ScreenIndexedGivingKey consults no edition. cite.py: OK §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR8 the text is in SR8.
